title: The Erdős Similarity Conjecture for Two-Fold Sumsets with a Geometric Summand
summary: We settle a major case in the two-set regime of the Erdős similarity conjecture: the sum of a geometric sequence and an arbitrary infinite set is never measure universal. Here a set $E\subset\R$ is measure universal if every measurable set of positive Lebesgue measure contains an affine copy of $E$. More precisely, if $A\subset\R$ is infinite, $a\neq 0$, and $0 0$, the stretched-exponential sumset \[ \{2^{-n^{α_1}}\}+\{2^{-n^{α_2}}\} \] is not measure universal whenever $1/α_1+1/α_2>1$; analogous conclusions hold for difference sets.
